solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/exactly-one-consecutive-set-bits-pair/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

3950. Exactly One Consecutive Set Bits Pair

You are given an integer n.

Return true if its binary representation contains exactly one adjacent pair of set bits, and false otherwise.

Example 1:

Input: n = 6
Output: true
Explanation:
- Binary representation of 6 is 110.
- There is exactly one adjacent pair of set bits ("11"). Thus, the answer is true.

Example 2:

Input: n = 5
Output: false
Explanation:
- Binary representation of 5 is 101.
- There is no adjacent pair of set bits. Thus, the answer is false.

Constraints:

    0 <= n <= 10^5
"""


class Solution:
    def consecutiveSetBits(self, n: int) -> bool:
        count = 0
        prev_bit = 0
        while n > 0:
            curr_bit = n & 1
            if curr_bit == 1 and prev_bit == 1:
                count += 1
            prev_bit = curr_bit
            n >>= 1
        return count == 1


sol = Solution()

print(sol.consecutiveSetBits(6))  # true

assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(6) == True
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(5) == False

assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(0) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(1) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(3) == True
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(7) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(15) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(31) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(21) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(85) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(1023) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(65535) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(100000) == False
assert sol.consecutiveSetBits(99999) == False
